title: Check agent login before dispatch and each stage; hold on expiry
summary: Add a login-validity probe run before a job is dispatched and before each agent stage. If the login is expired, or expires within the stage deadline, hold the job as an environment stop with a re-authenticate message and start no producer, modelled on the existing disk_gate/hold_for_disk path. Audience: whoever drains jobs and sees an environment hold instead of a mid-run 401.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require cargo test, clippy and fmt --check to pass.
Criterion checks the producer is never run on expired login.
The rule is enforced by a gate in code, with a test that fails without it.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (produce_and_verify, disk_gate and hold_for_disk run before the producer and hold the job as an environment stop with no candidate; producer_stop_reason in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs gives the environment reason for an expired login) and crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs (api_error_status classifies a 401; the driver retries it once after AUTH_RETRY_WAIT; tests use a shell stub with MODE=auth_always). Nothing checks the login before the producer starts. The new gate runs first in produce_and_verify and at dispatch, ahead of each agent stage, reusing the hold path and the 401 classifier.
Records validation: no new record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected; the hold reuses the existing environment-stop closing.

The login check is a trait or method on the agent driver so a stub can return expired, valid, or expiring-soon; the real implementation uses a cheap authenticated call or the credential's expiry time. The stage deadline comes from the existing per-stage timeout config.
The named file records/failure-classes/2026-10/20261028-112757-sygc.json is the failure-class evidence and is read-only; it is not a deliverable.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) are not changed; no new config key is added and the stage deadline reuses an existing value. Consumers: none found.
Environment: no CI workflow, push or PR is touched; tests run offline against stubs.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new login-validity check in crates/athena-agent/src/ (or the run module) returns expired when the login is expired or expires within the stage deadline; the diff shows it called in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs before the producer starts and before each agent stage, not only after a 401.

When the check fails, the job is held through the existing environment-stop path (like hold_for_disk), with a message telling the user to re-authenticate; the diff shows no candidate or resume mark is created.

A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs uses an expired-login stub; it asserts dispatch holds the job as an environment stop and the producer stub is never invoked (a call counter or marker stays zero). Run cargo test; the test passes, and fails if the gate call is removed.
A second test with a valid-login stub shows the producer still runs and the job proceeds as before. Run cargo test and see it pass.
Existing tests still pass and no unrelated behavior changes: run cargo test (the whole suite), cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check, each as its own command, and all pass.

CHANGELOG.md gains an entry for the change, and the new rule is stated in docs where hold rules are described, recorded as a new appended decision in docs/decisions.md with a Provenance bullet; no existing entry is edited.

out_of_scope: Changing the existing mid-run 401 retry behavior
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than reference: a pipeline gate touching dispatch and several stages needs a new stub test.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed attempts and wasted producer runs that end in a 401 mid-run.
hard_reason: Adds a gate that can hold jobs and changes the run pipeline's dispatch and stage order, so a mistake is costly.
